answer: A strong defence is to tie each agent reputation to a scarce, verifiable stake, like a bond locked in escrow. A new identity that behaves honestly slowly earns trust, while one that misbehaves loses its deposit — the cost of creating fake identities becomes as heavy as basalt, while genuine agents build a solid record like marble. The effect should ripple outward: peers share reputation signals, so a sybil swarm cannot hide behind fresh faces, because its history of forfeited bonds follows every copy it spawns.
